Exact three-dimensional panel coordinates

Source: R/coord-3d.R
coord_3d.Rd

Set z_scales = "free" here to train a separate z range per facet. ggplot2 facets control x and y scales and have no z scale.

Usage

coord_3d(
  projection = "orthographic",
  azimuth = -60,
  elevation = 30,
  roll = 0,
  oblique = c(angle = 45, ratio = 0.5),
  up = "z",
  distance = NULL,
  fov = 35,
  zoom = 1,
  target = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5),
  near = NULL,
  far = NULL,
  aspect = c(1, 1, 1),
  xlim = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  zlim = NULL,
  expand = TRUE,
  clip = "on",
  clip_data = TRUE,
  axes = c("x", "y", "z"),
  panes = c("back", "floor"),
  box = "back",
  z_scales = "fixed",
  crs = NULL,
  light = light_3d(),
  backend = backend_3d(),
  default = FALSE,
  frame = "view",
  transform = NULL,
  axis_lines = "box",
  origin = c(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0),
  clip_planes = list(),
  stereo = NULL,
  space = "euclidean",
  model = NULL,
  input = NULL,
  isometry = NULL,
  munch_tolerance = 0.001,
  munch_max_depth = 9L,
  shadow = NULL,
  depth_cue = NULL
)

Arguments

projection

"orthographic", "perspective" or "oblique". An oblique projection is parallel with a sight ray that is not perpendicular to the image: depth recedes on the page along oblique.

azimuth, elevation, roll

Camera angles in degrees.

oblique

Receding direction of an oblique projection: angle in degrees counterclockwise from the page's right, and ratio, the drawn length of one unit of depth.

up

Vertical axis, "x", "y" or "z". Azimuth turns about it and elevation rises toward it.

distance, fov, zoom

Camera distance, field of view and magnification. Each camera argument from azimuth to zoom takes one value, shared by all panels, or one value per panel in layout order, so facets can show the scene from different views.

target

Target fractions within the expanded box.

near, far

Camera clipping distances.

aspect

Three positive model side lengths, or "data".

xlim, ylim, zlim

Coordinate zoom limits in original units.

expand

Logical scalar or named x, y, z logical vector.

clip

Rectangular viewport clipping, on or off.

clip_data

Whether to clip to the data box.

axes

Axes to draw.

panes

Cube faces to draw: "back" (the rear pane of each pair of walls), "floor", "front" (the panes facing the viewer that are not drawn otherwise, styled by the theme element panel.pane.front and drawn over the data without grid lines), or pane names "xmin" to "zmax".

box

Box edges, back, all or none.

z_scales

Fixed or free z scales across panels.

crs

Target spatial coordinate reference system.

light

Lighting configuration or NULL.

backend

Backend configuration.

default

Whether this is the default coordinate system.

frame

Fit the current view, all azimuths at this elevation, or a sphere.

transform

Optional coordinate transformations applied after statistics, as a named list with entries x, y or z, each a transformation name such as "log10" or a scales transformation. Lines and faces are subdivided so their images bend with the transformation.

axis_lines

Where axis lines and their ticks and labels sit: "box" on an edge of the box, "origin" through the point origin, or "none", which keeps ticks and labels on the box edges and draws no axis lines. A guide with an explicit position (see guide_axis_3d()) keeps it. Origin axes, their ticks, tick labels and titles are part of the scene, so data in front of them hide them; the label at the point where origin axes cross is left out. Origin axis lines use the theme elements axis.line.origin.x, .y and .z, which inherit from axis.line.origin.

origin

Named numeric vector with entries x, y and z in data units, the point through which origin axes pass. Missing entries are 0. A value outside the panel range is moved to the nearest end of the range.

clip_planes

A list of clip_plane_3d() planes that cut every layer of the panel. A layer's own clip_planes argument replaces this list for that layer.

stereo

Stereo output from stereo_3d(), or NULL for one view.

space

Geometry of paths and faces: "euclidean" or an internal Space3D extension. Spaces define canonical points, chart conversions, distance, geodesics and isometries. See Details.

model

Display model supplied by the space; NULL uses its default.

input

Input chart supplied by the space; NULL uses model.

isometry

Optional space-specific action on canonical points.

munch_tolerance

Positive chord-error tolerance in projected panel fractions, used for geodesic subdivision. The default is 0.001.

munch_max_depth

Maximum binary subdivision depth, from 0 to 12. A space reports an error when this budget cannot meet the tolerance.

shadow

Planar cast shadows from shadow_3d(), or NULL for none.

depth_cue

Fog, depth-thinned strokes and eye-dome lighting from depth_cue_3d(), or NULL for none.

Value

A Coord3D ggproto object.

Details

Space extensions inherit from ggplot3d:::Space3D. They declare charts, models and default_model, and implement to_canonical(data, chart), from_canonical(X, model), distance(X, Y), geodesic(X, Y, s) and act(g, X). Canonical points are finite numeric row matrices of any dimension. Geodesic endpoints are paired rows and s is a scalar or one parameter per row, from zero to one. Input positions are scale-transformed chart coordinates. Model output has three columns in model axis units; model_ranges(model, panel_params) supplies named x, y, z bounds. Four-column homogeneous output (x, y, z, w) with w >= 0 is also accepted and travels unchanged into the scene packet; w = 0 is a point at infinity. Projective models such as the Klein ball return (X, X0), so clipping to the panel box happens in homogeneous coordinates before division (Blinn and Newell 1978) and isometries stay linear. An edge whose image passes through infinity carries its ideal point as an explicit corner.

chart_is_projective(model) declares straight geodesic images and planar faces, allowing subdivision to be omitted. Other models share the frame subdivision machinery, sampling geodesics before projection. Faces use nested geodesic interpolation on a triangular lattice; shared edges use identical canonical samples. Continuous paint attributes interpolate by geodesic parameter, with piecewise constant paint on emitted primitives. Discrete attributes and source identities follow the starting corner. Polygon topology is triangulated in a planar input chart; curved models receive those triangles and closed boundary strokes. Panel furniture is supplied by the frame. Visibility is exact for the resulting tessellation.

Theme elements

Besides the ggplot2 elements, panels read these theme elements:

  • panel.pane, panel.pane.x, panel.pane.y, panel.pane.z: pane fills, by the axis normal to the pane; panel.pane.front styles the panes selected with panes = "front".

  • panel.grid.major.x.xy, panel.grid.minor.z.yz and so on: the grid lines of one axis on the panes of one plane. Each inherits from the grid element of its axis (panel.grid.major.x.xy from panel.grid.major.x), so element_blank() removes those lines from that plane only. In the default view the floor is the xy plane.

  • panel.zero.x, panel.zero.y, panel.zero.z: a plane through the panel at transformed value 0 of that axis, when 0 lies inside the range. They are blank by default; setting one to an ggplot2::element_rect() draws it, filled from panel.zero. Zero planes are part of the scene, so they hide data behind them.

  • panel.zero.line.x, .y, .z, inheriting from panel.zero.line (blank by default): the line at transformed value 0 on each drawn pane.

  • panel.box.back, panel.box.front: box edges.

  • axis.line.origin.x, .y, .z: origin axis lines.

  • panel.margin.3d: the margin around the projected box.

Examples

d <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c(1, 3, 2), z = c(2, 1, 3))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 3) + coord_3d(azimuth = -45, elevation = 25)
d$site <- c("a", "a", "b")
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_point_3d() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~site) + coord_3d(z_scales = "free")
views <- rbind(transform(d, view = "front"), transform(d, view = "side"))
ggplot2::ggplot(views, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_point_3d() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~view) + coord_3d(azimuth = c(-60, 30))
centred <- data.frame(x = c(-2, 1, 2), y = c(1, -2, 2), z = c(-1, 2, 1))
ggplot2::ggplot(centred, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_point_3d(size = 3) +
  coord_3d(axis_lines = "origin", panes = "floor") +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.zero.z = ggplot2::element_rect(),
    panel.zero.line = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "grey30"))
ggplot2::ggplot(centred, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_point_3d(size = 3) +
  coord_3d(panes = c("back", "floor", "front")) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.major.z.xz = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    panel.pane.front = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#4682B41A"))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_point_3d() +
  coord_3d(clip_planes = list(clip_plane_3d(c(0, 0, -1), c(z = 2.5))))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_point_3d() +
  coord_3d(stereo = stereo_3d("cross"))
rotation <- diag(4)
rotation[1:2, 1:2] <- matrix(c(0, 1, -1, 0), 2)
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_path_3d() +
  coord_3d(isometry = rotation, xlim = c(-4, 4), ylim = c(-4, 4))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_point_3d(size = 4) +
  coord_3d(shadow = shadow_3d(), depth_cue = depth_cue_3d())
